issue: Does the First Step Act's retroactivity provision (§ 404) cover a defendant whose sentence for a covered offense was imposed before the Act's effective date but later vacated, or does the earlier sentence count as 'a sentence' imposed as a matter of historical fact, barring relief?
provision: First Step Act of 2018, Pub. L. 115-391, § 404

sides.position: A sentence imposed before the Act's effective date counts as 'a sentence' as a matter of historical fact even if it was later vacated, so the defendant is not eligible for § 404 relief.
cases: United States v. Jackson, 995 F.3d 511 (6th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Carpenter, 80 F.4th 790 (6th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: A sentence that was vacated does not bar § 404 relief, so the defendant may seek a reduced sentence under the Act's retroactivity provision.
cases: United States v. Mitchell, 38 F.4th 382 (3d Cir. 2022)
United States v. Merrell, 36 F.4th 571 (9th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Bethea, 841 F. App'x 544 (4th Cir. 2021)

this_court: The Sixth Circuit, through Jackson and this denial of en banc review, holds that a pre-Act sentence counts as 'a sentence' even if vacated, so the defendant is not eligible for § 404 relief.
quote: Jackson also splits from all our sister circuits to have reached the question.
cite: United States v. Timothy Carpenter, 80 F.4th 790 (6th Cir. 2023)
